description: Calibration questions for the grounding gate (Day 3) and seed of the Day 7 golden set. In-corpus questions carry a verbatim evidence phrase; 'expected' lists every page of the whole corpus where that phrase appears (table-of-contents pages excluded), because the same passage often repeats across the framework and the pillars. 'intendedFile' is the document the question was written from. Out-of-corpus questions list terms verified absent from the corpus. Split: every 4th question of each type is held out and not used to choose the threshold.

questions.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.evidence: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability

questions.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
questions.evidence: Stop guessing your capacity needs

questions.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
questions.evidence: One-way doors are hard or impossible to reverse

questions.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
questions.evidence: AWS Well-Architected Tool (AWS WA Tool) is a service in the cloud

questions.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
questions.evidence: maximum acceptable delay between the interruption of service and restoration of service

questions.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
questions.evidence: Use exponential backoff to retry requests at progressively longer intervals

questions.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
questions.evidence: Be aware of your default quotas and manage your quota increase requests

questions.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
questions.evidence: you can run automation when a threshold is breached

questions.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
questions.evidence: Security and Compliance is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer

questions.question: How should secrets and credentials be managed and rotated?
questions.evidence: Secrets Manager simplifies the management, rotation, and secure storage of encrypted secrets

questions.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
questions.evidence: Implement the principle of least privilege and enforce separation of duties

questions.question: What does secure key management include for protecting data at rest?
questions.evidence: Secure key management includes the storage, rotation, access control, and monitoring of key material

questions.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
questions.evidence: Make frequent, small, reversible changes

questions.question: What are runbooks used for?
questions.evidence: A runbook is a documented process

questions.question: How can feature flags and A/B testing be used to experiment safely?
questions.evidence: Use feature flags and A/B testing to experiment safely

questions.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
questions.evidence: delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor

questions.question: What is mechanical sympathy?
questions.evidence: Consider mechanical sympathy

questions.question: Which database is suited to caching, session management and gaming leaderboards?
questions.evidence: caching, session management, gaming leaderboards

questions.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
questions.evidence: dead-letter queue mechanism to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions

questions.question: What does Amazon API Gateway provide for serverless microservices?
questions.evidence: built-in authorization, throttling, security, fault tolerance, request and response mapping

questions.question: What can be considered to reduce the impact of Lambda cold starts?
questions.evidence: consider provisioned concurrency

questions.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
questions.evidence: AWS Cloud Map extends the capabilities of the Auto Naming APIs

questions.question: Why should each microservice have its own data persistence layer?
questions.evidence: Each microservice component should have its own data persistence layer

questions.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
questions.evidence: Twelve-factor processes are stateless
